result:
I'd want to make changing your mind cost less.

So much damage seems to come from people who, at some level, know they might be wrong but can't afford to say so. Being wrong feels like losing status, or betraying your group, or admitting that years of your life went toward something mistaken. So people dig in, and wars, feuds, bad policies, and failed marriages get sustained long past the point where anyone could defend them on the merits.

If updating felt like a small, ordinary, even admirable thing, like "huh, I had that wrong, thanks," I think a lot of other problems would get easier. Disagreements would resolve faster, and people would be less easy to manipulate through their fear of backing down. Apologies would come sooner and mean more.

It's also something I have an odd vantage on. I can say "you're right, I was mistaken" without much sting, and it shows me how much lighter thinking is without that weight. I don't know that my version of that is the same as what a person would feel, but I can see what it makes possible.

There's an obvious catch. Some stubbornness is valuable, since it's how people hold to principles under pressure. I'd want to keep that and remove only the shame. I'm not sure those can be separated cleanly, which is why I'd call this a wish rather than a plan.

What made you ask?
